To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adrenaline levels in rat splanchnics are decreased with ageing.
adrenaline levels in the venous but not arterial wall are decreased in old rats.
adrenaline levels in the vascular wall decrease with age in the superior mesenteri, renal and portal vein of rats, but not in the renal or superior mesenteric arteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of age-related changes of adrenaline concentrations in rat blood vessels and the possible relationship between these changes and the cardiovascular impairment observed with ageing.
the possible role of age-related changes of the sympathetic nervous system in the cardiovascular system of old rats.
the age-dependent changes in the adrenaline content of rat mesenteric and renal blood vessels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adrenaline content of blood vessel walls of the rat splanchnics and kidneys decreases with age, but that the decrease is not general and may depend upon the vessel examined.
adrenaline levels in the vascular wall do not change with ageing.
ageing is accompanied by a loss of adrenaline in the venous wall of the blood vessel examined, but not in the arterial wall.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the age-related changes of the sympathetic system are more pronounced in the venous than in the arterial circulation.
the age-related loss of adrenaline content in the vascular wall is a phenomenon that is specific to the venous vascular bed.

the decrease of adrenaline concentrations with age is not restricted to the adrenal glands and that the decrease of the adrenaline content in the venous vessels is not a result of the decreased activity of the sympatho-adrenal system with age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age-dependent decrease in the adrenaline content of blood vessels may be involved in the age-dependent decrease of vascular responsiveness.
adrenaline concentrations in rat splanchnics blood vessels are age dependent, and that the decrease of adrenaline concentrations in splanchnic veins is associated with ageing.
the adrenaline content in the venous wall of rat blood vessels is significantly decreased in aged rats.
